messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: minor thing
parts:
J

In the print() output from rstan, instead of Mean, SE.Mean, SD, … , ESS, Rhat,
let's change to mean, se_mean, sd, …, n_eff, Rhat.
I prefer lower case (except for Rhat, which is special), and also we should be consistent with Stan and use underscore rather than dot as a separator. Finally, I prefer n_eff to ESS, because ESS in R can remind people of Emacs Speaks Statistics which is a distraction.

Also, can we add another line where we automatically save and summarize the log posterior (as computed by the model, up to an arbitrary normalizing constant)? R2WinBUGS computed deviance but that's more complicated as it needs to know which parts of the model are the prior and which are the likelihood. For now let's just keep things simple and save log posterior.

Thx
A

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: dots vs. underscores in R variable names
parts:
On 8/25/12 11:33 PM, Jiqiang Guo wrote:
> I will make the changes soon.
> Taking about dot and underscor, do you want all dots that users will encounter such as parameter names for function
> stan and some function names to be replaced?

I think it's OK to go with dots in function
names and parameter names in R. Whatever
R users are most used to.

The stanc parser will catch any dots in models
and warn users accordingly. Data and initial values
will then have to match, so those shouldn't contain
any dots.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: dots vs. underscores in R variable names
parts:
On Sunday, August 26, 2012 6:39:37 PM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
On 8/25/12 11:33 PM, Jiqiang Guo wrote:
> I will make the changes soon.
> Taking about dot and underscor, do you want all  dots that users will encounter such as parameter names for function
> stan and some function names to be replaced?

I think it's OK to go with dots in function
names and parameter names in R.  Whatever
R users are most used to.

For function *arguments*, periods are not the worst thing in the world. For function *names*, periods are pretty bad because periods are also used to indicate methods of S3 generic functions, e.g. mean.matrix() is the function that gets called by mean() when passed a matrix. It is unfortunate that R did this for 10 years so that people got used to it, and unfortunate that ESS was written when underscores were illegal in the R language so that pressing underscore results in the <- sign. But I personally don't put periods in function names ever.

Ben

messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] dots vs. underscores in R variable names
parts:
I don't want dots in data names or parameter names in R. Why do I say this? Because we are typically passing data straight from R to Stan, and passing parameters straight from Stan to R. It will be a recipe for confusion if we have data or parameter that's called sigma.y in R and sigma_y in Stan. Better to go with sigma_y in both.

A

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] dots vs. underscores in R variable names
parts:
We're talking about arguments to the stan() function,
not model parameters.

So things like n.burnin and n.thin in R2WinBugs.

I'd just as soon not use dots myself. I find
them very confusing. Ben made a very good case
for not using them for function names at least.

It would probably be simplest to just match the
command-line argument names. Here they are,
as printed by the --help option:

--help Display this information

--data=<file> Read data from specified dump-format file
(required if model declares data)

--init=<file> Use initial values from specified file or zero values if <file>=0
(default is random initialization)

--samples=<file> File into which samples are written
(default = samples.csv)

--append_samples Append samples to existing file if it exists
(does not write header in append mode)

--seed=<int> Random number generation seed
(default = randomly generated from time)

--chain_id=<int> Markov chain identifier
(default = 1)

--iter=<+int> Total number of iterations, including warmup
(default = 2000)

--warmup=<+int> Discard the specified number of initial samples
(default = iter / 2)

--thin=<+int> Period between saved samples after warm up
(default = max(1, floor(iter - warmup) / 1000))

--refresh=<+int> Period between samples updating progress report print
(default = max(1,iter/200)))

--leapfrog_steps=<int>
Number of leapfrog steps; -1 for No-U-Turn adaptation
(default = -1)

--max_treedepth=<int>
Limit NUTS leapfrog steps to 2^max_tree_depth; -1 for no limit
(default = 10)

--epsilon=<float> Initial value for step size, or -1 to set automatically
(default = -1)

--epsilon_pm=<[0,1]>
Sample epsilon +/- epsilon * epsilon_pm
(default = 0.0)

--equal_step_sizes Use same step size for every parameter with NUTS
(default is to estimate varying step sizes during warmup)

--delta=<+float> Initial step size for step-size adaptation
(default = 0.5)

--gamma=<+float> Gamma parameter for dual averaging step-size adaptation
(default = 0.05)

--save_warmup Save the warmup samples

--test_grad Test gradient calculations using finite differences


- Bob
